title: Ad Hoc Relational Engines and Unindexed Application-Side Joins
pattern: Application code recreates relational tables, lookup joins, indexes, or transaction machinery in memory instead of using an appropriate query engine. This covers both full emulated engines (ad-hoc tabular layouts, manual rollbacks, hand-built indexes) and the narrower case of nested-loop ID joins across collections.
why_bad: The application assumes database implementation responsibilities: it recreates a fragile, non-durable engine that bypasses standard query optimizers and index caching, performs quadratic (\(O(n \cdot m)\)) joins, retains excessive memory, and implements brittle persistence/transaction behavior.
detection: Either of: (1) nested arrays or maps that encode table schemas or relational schema matrices, paired with manual lookup loops that simulate relational joins; or (2) nested iteration loops over collections that repeatedly match records by ID variables with avoidable multiplicative cost. Hand-built indexing or rollback machinery attached to such structures is part of the emulated engine, but a lone map or index is not by itself a violation.
counterexample: Small bounded collection operations using an appropriate algorithm (e.g. a single indexed lookup); purpose-built in-memory query engines; **Unit Testing Mocks:** short-lived, read-only structures used to mock external datastores inside test files, as long as they do not recreate a relational engine or duplicate relational join operations.
source: Martin Kleppmann - _Designing Data-Intensive Applications_ The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems_ (2017, O’Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 2 "Relational Model vs. Document Model"; [Robert C. Martin Series] Robert C. Martin - _Clean Architecture_ A Craftsman’s Guide to Software Structure and Design_ (2017, Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 17 "InMemoryPage".
